matter_reference_date_basis: exam_session 'APRIL 2020' recorded in candidates/matters/M069.json; the law is taken as it stood in April 2020.
corpus_gaps: The Second Schedule to the Registration of Documents Ordinance (the prescribed forms, including the priority notice form referred to by section 50) is not in the frozen corpus. Only section 50's instruction to use those forms is present, and the only Schedule form text in the corpus is the caveat form substituted by Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022 s.5, which post-dates the matter date and concerns caveats, not priority notices.

The regulations made under section 49 prescribing the manner of presentation, the day-book particulars (section 27) and the Registrar's endorsement form (section 43(2)) are not in the corpus, so the exact wording and formal parts a Land Registry expects on the notice cannot be verified.

The First Schedule fee payable on registering a priority notice is not reproduced in the corpus; Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2013 s.5 amends items of that Schedule but the Schedule itself was not extracted.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Any person (in this section called a " transferee") acquiring or proposing to acquire for valuable consideration from any other person (in this section called the " transferor") any interest or benefit in any land may before the execution of the instrument by the transferor with his written consent, or after the execution of the instrument by the transferor without such consent, present for registration a notice (in this Ordinance called a " priority notice ") of his intention to register the instrument.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; no amendment to section 30 appears in the corpus. The Registration of Documents (Amendment) Acts in the corpus that post-date the matter (No. 32 of 2022, No. 18 of 2024) touch sections 8, 25, 29, 32, 33, 41, 50 and the Schedules, not section 30.
provisions.why_relevant: This is the provision that creates the notice the Bank asked for: a priority notice of the transferee's intention to register the instrument. It fixes who the parties to the notice are (transferee and transferor), that the acquisition must be for valuable consideration, and whether the transferor's written consent must appear on the face of the notice (needed if it is lodged before execution of the deed, not needed after).

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The Registrar shall, on receiving a priority notice, register it in the same manner as other instruments, but shall retain the notice.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; unamended in the corpus as at April 2020.
provisions.why_relevant: This is the bridge between the priority notice and the ordinary presentation rules. Because the Registrar registers the notice 'in the same manner as other instruments', the drafting requirements that apply to instruments presented for registration (section 13(1) description of land, section 13(7) folio reference at the head) govern the notice as well, and because the Registrar retains the notice a duplicate must be tendered for endorsement.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every instrument (except a will) presented for registration shall contain embodied therein, or in a schedule annexed thereto, an accurate and clear description of the land affected thereby, its boundaries, extent, and situation specifying the district and the village, pattu, korale, or other division of the district in which the land is situated; and in case the land is situated in any town, the name, if any, of the street in which it is situated.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927. The corpus records a 1982 change to section 13 (Registration of Documents No. 50 of 1982 s.2) and Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2013 s.5 amends only the fee words in subsection (6). Subsection (1) as reproduced in the consolidated text was in force in April 2020.
provisions.why_relevant: Supplies the content of the schedule to the drafted notice: the land must be described by boundaries, extent and situation, with the district and the division, and (the premises being in a town) the name of the street. It is why the draft cannot simply say 'Assessment No. 23, 1st Lane, Ratmalana' but must add boundaries, extent and district.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: There shall be typewritten or written in ink at the head of every instrument (except a will) presented for registration a reference to the volume and folio in which some earlier instrument relating to the same land is registered
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; the corpus shows no change to subsection (7) before April 2020.
provisions.why_relevant: Explains the Bank's instruction to submit the notice 'together with the folio': the volume and folio in which an earlier instrument affecting the same land is registered must appear at the head of the document presented for registration.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The forms contained in the Second Schedule shall be used with such variations as circumstances may require, but such Schedule may be altered or added to by regulation.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927. Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022 s.4 amends section 50 and s.5 replaces a Second Schedule form, but both post-date April 2020 and are not applied here.
provisions.why_relevant: A drafting answer must reproduce the statutory form. Section 50 makes the Second Schedule form mandatory (subject to variation as circumstances require), and that Schedule is not in the corpus, so the prescribed wording of the priority notice cannot be verified from the frozen corpus. This is the provision that blocks the question.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: A priority notice shall remain in force for six weeks from the date of registration of the notice
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; unamended in the corpus as at April 2020.
provisions.why_relevant: Fixes the currency of the notice and therefore the date the draft must carry and the deadline within which the transfer deed and mortgage bond must be executed and registered; it also supports a renewal clause where the six weeks are likely to run out.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: any person claiming any interest or benefit thereunder; (c) any person having any interest in or charge on any property affected thereby; or (d) the agent of any such person or a attorney-at-law or notary acting on behalf of any such person.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; unamended in the corpus as at April 2020.
provisions.why_relevant: Identifies who may sign and present the notice at the Land Registry, so the draft may be subscribed by the transferee himself or by the notary or attorney-at-law acting for him.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: An endorsement by the Registrar in the prescribed form on a duplicate of an application for registration of a lis pendens, or on a duplicate of a priority notice or seizure priority notice or an application for renewal of such a notice, or on a duplicate of a caveat shall be admissible in evidence without proof of the signature or appointment of the Registrar

provisions.why_relevant: Shows that the notice is tendered in duplicate: the Registrar retains the original under section 30(4) and endorses the duplicate, and that endorsed duplicate is the proof of registration the Bank will want before releasing the loan.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: If, at any time while a priority notice remains in force, any instrument is registered whereby the transferee or a person deriving title under him acquires for valuable consideration from the transferor or a person deriving title under him any interest or benefit in the land described in the priority notice, such instrument shall, for the purposes of this Ordinance, be deemed to have been registered at the time of registration of the priority notice.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; unamended in the corpus as at April 2020.
provisions.why_relevant: Background to the drafting task: it is this back-dating effect that makes the notice worth lodging and that explains why the instrument the notice describes must be identified accurately in the draft.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The document asked for is a creature of statute. Section 30 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance creates the priority notice and states who lodges it against whom and on what condition, sections 13(1) and 13(7) fix the description of the land and the folio reference, section 26(1) says who may present it and section 50 makes the Second Schedule form the form to be used. No judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed to draft it. The gap is not that the authority is non-statutory but that one statutory component, the Second Schedule form, is absent from the frozen corpus, which is why the question is blocked rather than reserved.

legal_issues.issue: Which statutory notice does the Bank's instruction refer to, and what does the Ordinance require that notice to contain: the parties, the interest acquired for valuable consideration, the instrument intended to be registered, and the transferor's written consent where the notice is lodged before execution.

Which presentation rules apply to the drafted notice, given that section 30(4) directs the Registrar to register it in the same manner as other instruments: the schedule describing the land under section 13(1), the volume and folio reference at the head under section 13(7), signature and presentation under section 26(1), and a duplicate for endorsement under section 43(2).
Whether the prescribed form of the notice can be reproduced from the frozen corpus, section 50 requiring the Second Schedule form to be used with such variations as circumstances may require.

Whether the notice to be drafted is the one Gamini Perera lodges as transferee against his vendor, or the one the Mortgage Bank lodges as transferee against Gamini Perera in respect of the bond, the background naming only 'a certain Notice' and directing Gamini Perera to register it.

questions.hop_count_basis: Three necessary linked steps: section 30(1) creates the notice and fixes its parties and consent condition; section 30(4) carries it into the ordinary registration regime; and that in turn imports the drafting requirements of section 13(1) and 13(7), with section 50 requiring the Second Schedule form. Only these dependencies are counted; sections 26(1), 43(2) and 30(5) add detail without which the draft would still stand.

enrichment.original_background: Gamini Perera intends to purchase a house and property situated in Ratmalana bearing Assessment No. 23, 1st Lane, Ratmalana. He applied for a loan from the Mortgage Bank and the Bank approved his Loan and informed him to get a certain Notice registered in the Land Registry and submit together with the folio in order to release the Loan on the simultaneous execution of the Transfer Deed and the Mortgage Bond without awaiting the completion of registration formalities.

gold_answer_draft.issue: How is the notice the Bank asked for to be drawn up and presented to the Land Registry? The notice is the priority notice under section 30 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, and the question is what its parties, recitals, schedule and formal parts must be so that the transfer deed and the mortgage bond, when executed, are deemed registered as at the date the notice was registered.
gold_answer_draft.rule: A person acquiring or proposing to acquire an interest in land for valuable consideration (the transferee) may present for registration a notice of his intention to register the instrument, which the Ordinance calls a priority notice; if the notice is lodged before the transferor executes the instrument it must carry the transferor's written consent, and if lodged afterwards it need not (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.30(1)). While the notice is in force, an instrument by which the transferee acquires the interest described in it is deemed to have been registered at the time the notice was registered (s.30(2)). The Registrar registers the notice in the same manner as other instruments and retains it (s.30(4)), so the notice must contain, embodied in it or in a schedule annexed to it, an accurate and clear description of the land with its boundaries, extent and situation, the district and division and, the land being in a town, the street (s.13(1)), and it must carry at its head, typewritten or in ink, a reference to the volume and folio in which an earlier instrument relating to the same land is registered (s.13(7)). It may be signed and presented by the transferee, by any person claiming an interest or benefit under the instrument, or by a notary or attorney-at-law acting for him (s.26(1)); it should be tendered in duplicate, because the Registrar retains the original (s.30(4)) and his endorsement on the duplicate is prima facie evidence of registration (s.43(2)). The notice remains in force for six weeks from the date of its registration and may be renewed once for a further six weeks (s.30(5)). By s.50 the form contained in the Second Schedule to the Ordinance is to be used, with such variations as circumstances may require.
gold_answer_draft.application: Gamini Perera is a person proposing to acquire for valuable consideration an interest in the house and premises bearing Assessment No. 23, 1st Lane, Ratmalana, so he is a transferee within s.30(1) and his vendor is the transferor. Because the Bank wants the loan released on simultaneous execution of the transfer deed and the mortgage bond without awaiting completion of registration, the notice has to be lodged before those deeds are executed, and it must therefore carry the vendor's written consent (s.30(1)). The instrument whose intended registration is notified is the deed of transfer to be executed by the vendor in his favour; the Bank's own security is covered by a corresponding notice in which the Bank is the transferee and Gamini Perera the transferor in respect of the mortgage bond. The premises being in a town, the schedule must give the street, the boundaries and the extent as well as the assessment number (s.13(1)), and the folio the Bank asked him to submit gives the volume and folio reference to be written at the head of the notice (s.13(7)). A draft on these lines reads: at the head, 'Registered in Volume ...... Folio ...... of the ...... Land Registry'; then 'PRIORITY NOTICE UNDER SECTION 30 OF THE REGISTRATION OF DOCUMENTS ORDINANCE. To the Registrar of Lands, ...... Land Registry. Take notice that I, Gamini Perera of ......, propose to acquire for valuable consideration from ...... of ...... the land and premises described in the Schedule hereto, and that I intend to register the deed of transfer to be executed by the said ...... in my favour in respect of the said premises. I present this notice before the execution of the said instrument, with the written consent of the said transferor endorsed below. Dated this ...... day of ...... . [Signature of transferee, or of the notary or attorney-at-law presenting it under s.26(1)]. I, ......, the transferor above named, consent in writing to the registration of this notice. [Signature of transferor]. THE SCHEDULE: All that house and premises bearing Assessment No. 23, 1st Lane, Ratmalana, in the ...... Ward of ......, in the ...... Division of the District of Colombo, Western Province, bounded on the North by ......, on the East by ......, on the South by ......, and on the West by ......, and containing in extent ...... .' The notice is tendered in duplicate so that the Registrar, who retains the original, endorses registration on the duplicate for the Bank (ss.30(4), 43(2)), and it must be acted on within the six weeks it remains in force (s.30(5)).
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The notice to be drafted is a priority notice under section 30 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, drawn as above with the transferor's written consent, a section 13(1) schedule of the land and the section 13(7) volume and folio reference at its head, presented in duplicate. The draft is not offered as a settled gold answer: section 50 requires the form in the Second Schedule to be used, that Schedule is not in the frozen corpus, and the background does not say whether the notice wanted is the purchaser's against his vendor or the Bank's against the purchaser. The wording above is therefore reconstructed from the operative sections only and needs the prescribed form and a lawyer's confirmation before it is treated as the model answer.

answer_claims.claim_text: The notice referred to is a priority notice, that is, a notice by a transferee acquiring or proposing to acquire an interest in land for valuable consideration of his intention to register the instrument.
A priority notice lodged before the transferor executes the instrument must carry the transferor's written consent; one lodged after execution need not.

Because the Registrar registers a priority notice in the same manner as other instruments and retains it, the notice must be drawn with a schedule giving an accurate and clear description of the land with its boundaries, extent, situation, district and division and, the land being in a town, the street.
A reference to the volume and folio in which an earlier instrument relating to the same land is registered must be typewritten or written in ink at the head of the notice.

The notice may be signed and presented by the transferee, by a person claiming an interest or benefit under the instrument, or by a notary or attorney-at-law acting for him, and should be tendered in duplicate so that the Registrar's endorsement of registration is available as evidence.

The notice carries a date and is effective for six weeks from its registration, renewable once for a further six weeks, so the transfer deed and bond must be executed and registered within that period.
The form to be used is the form contained in the Second Schedule to the Ordinance, with such variations as circumstances may require.

Gamini Perera, proposing to buy the premises at Assessment No. 23, 1st Lane, Ratmalana with bank finance, is a transferee within section 30(1), and his vendor is the transferor whose written consent the notice must bear if it is lodged before the deeds are executed.

The folio the Bank asked him to submit with the notice supplies the volume and folio reference that goes at the head of the notice, and the premises being in a town the schedule must state the street as well as the boundaries and extent.

Lodging the notice is what allows the Bank to release the loan on simultaneous execution of the transfer deed and the mortgage bond without awaiting registration, because an instrument registered while the notice is in force is deemed registered as at the date the notice was registered.

The notice should therefore be drafted as a priority notice under section 30, headed with the volume and folio, reciting the transferee, the transferor, the intended instrument and the transferor's written consent, subscribed and dated, with a schedule describing the premises, and presented in duplicate.
The drafted wording cannot be certified as the prescribed form, because section 50 requires the Second Schedule form to be used and that Schedule is not in the frozen corpus.

questions.block_reason: The question asks for a drafted document, and section 50 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance requires the form in the Second Schedule to be used with such variations as circumstances may require. That Second Schedule is not in the frozen corpus (the only Schedule form text present is the caveat form substituted by Act No. 32 of 2022 s.5, which both post-dates April 2020 and concerns caveats), nor are the section 49 regulations prescribing the manner of presentation and the Registrar's endorsement form. The substantive content of the notice is fully recoverable from sections 30(1), 30(4), 30(5), 13(1), 13(7), 26(1) and 43(2) and is drafted above, but the prescribed wording cannot be verified. A second, smaller obstacle: the background says only that the Bank told Gamini Perera to register 'a certain Notice', so whether the required draft is the purchaser's notice against his vendor or the Bank's notice against the purchaser in respect of the mortgage bond is not settled by the facts, and this is a 'keep' question so the facts were not enriched to settle it.
